title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal II
statement:
You are given `root`, the root of a binary tree. Group the node values by depth, listing each depth's values from left to right, and return these groups ordered from the deepest level up to the root's level (the root's group comes last).

Return an empty list when the tree has no nodes.
constraints: The tree has between 0 and 2000 nodes.
notes:
## Intuition

This is an ordinary level-order traversal with the final list of levels flipped. A breadth-first sweep naturally visits nodes one depth at a time, and within a depth from left to right, which is exactly the grouping asked for. Collect the levels top-down, then reverse them once at the end; inserting each level at the front instead would cost O(levels) per insert.

## Approach

1. If `root` is missing, return the empty `levels` list.
2. Keep the nodes of the current depth in `current`, starting with `[root]`.
3. For each node in `current`, add its value to `values` and push its existing children, left first, onto `next`.
4. Append `values` to `levels` and move on with `current = next` until a depth has no nodes.
5. Return `levels` reversed so the deepest level comes first.

## Example 1, step by step

For `[3, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7]`: `current = [3]` gives `values = [3]` and `next = [9, 20]`. Then `[9, 20]` gives `values = [9, 20]` and `next = [15, 7]` (9 has no children). Then `[15, 7]` gives `values = [15, 7]` and an empty `next`. `levels` is `[[3], [9, 20], [15, 7]]`, and reversing it returns `[[15, 7], [9, 20], [3]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is visited once, and the final reverse touches each level once.
- Space: O(n): the output holds every value, and `current`/`next` hold at most one level.

## Pitfalls

- Reverse the order of the levels, not the values inside each level; each group still reads left to right.
- Handle the empty tree before reading `root.val`.
- Push the left child before the right child, or the groups come out mirrored.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `levels` | the value groups collected from the root downward |
| `current` | nodes at the depth being processed |
| `next` | children found for the following depth |
| `values` | values of `current`, left to right |
| `node` | the node being read |

narration.2: Collect one list of values per depth, starting from the root's depth.
narration.3: An empty tree has no levels at all.
narration.6: The first depth holds only the root.
narration.7: Keep going while the current depth has at least one node.
narration.10: Visit this depth's nodes from left to right.
narration.11: Record the node's value in this depth's group.
narration.12: A left child belongs to the next depth, before any right child.
narration.15: The right child joins the next depth after the left one.
narration.19: This depth is complete; store its values.
narration.20: Move down to the children gathered for the next depth.
narration.22: Levels were gathered top-down, so reverse them to put the deepest first.
